decision: Introduce 5p charge for single-use carrier bags
claim_at_time: Government said the charge could reduce usage by as much as 80 percent in large supermarkets.
evidence_summary: Usage at the main retailers fell by more than 98 percent compared with the pre-charge baseline.
interpretation: The observed reduction ultimately exceeded the government's original up-to-80-percent expectation.

decision: Introduce minimum unit pricing for alcohol
claim_at_time: Modelling projected approximately a 3.5 percent reduction in alcohol consumption after introduction of minimum unit pricing.
evidence_summary: Evaluation found an approximately 3.5 percent reduction in alcohol purchases attributable to minimum unit pricing.
interpretation: Observed consumption reduction was broadly consistent with the original modelled estimate.

decision: Introduce minimum unit pricing for alcohol
claim_at_time: Pre-implementation modelling projected a reduction in alcohol-attributable deaths after minimum unit pricing.
evidence_summary: Evaluation estimated a 13.4 percent reduction in alcohol-attributable deaths following implementation.
interpretation: The estimated mortality reduction was larger than the earlier modelled expectation.

decision: Introduce the Soft Drinks Industry Levy
claim_at_time: The levy was designed to encourage manufacturers to reformulate drinks and reduce sugar content.
evidence_summary: Average sugar content in drinks subject to the levy fell substantially after announcement and implementation.
interpretation: The policy objective of encouraging substantial reformulation was strongly reflected in observed outcomes.

decision: Introduce the Soft Drinks Industry Levy
claim_at_time: Budget 2016 expected the Soft Drinks Industry Levy to raise about £520 million in its first full year.
evidence_summary: Revenue was substantially below the original forecast, in part because manufacturers reformulated products and therefore reduced exposure to the levy.
interpretation: The revenue forecast overestimated receipts, while the behavioral response encouraged by the policy reduced the tax base.

decision: Expand ULEZ across all London boroughs
claim_at_time: Expansion was expected to reduce road-transport emissions and improve roadside air quality across outer London.
evidence_summary: One-year evaluation estimated outer-London roadside NO2 concentrations about 4.8 percent lower than the modelled no-expansion counterfactual.
interpretation: Observed air-quality measures moved in the intended direction, although attribution relies on counterfactual modelling.
